rationale: Use own colour and coordinates modulo 3. Zeros in rows congruent to 0 become 8 in columns congruent to 1 or 2; zeros in rows congruent to 2 become 2 or 5 respectively. Demonstration 6 shows row 2 becoming [2,2,5,2,2,5].

Use own colour and the row's nonzero colour set. Rows containing only 2 fill zeros with 2; rows containing {2,3} recolour 3 to 4; rows containing {1,2,3} recolour zeros to 6 and 3 to 8, as demonstrated by [1,3,2,0] becoming [1,8,2,6].

Use own colour and the row's nonzero colour set. Zeros become 4 for {1,2}, and 7 for {2} or {1,3}; 3 becomes 0 for {1,2,3}. Demonstration 4 fills the zeros of [0,0,2,0,0] with 7, while demonstration 1 fills [0,2,0,0,0,1] with 4.

Use own colour and zero-based row and column parity. On even rows, odd-column zeros become 4 and 2 becomes 1, while even-column 3 becomes 0. On odd rows, even-column 2 becomes 4. Demonstration 1 exhibits all these changes.

Use own colour and zero-based coordinate parity. Even-row odd-column zeros become 2; even-row even-column 3 becomes 1; odd-row even-column zeros become 9 and 2 becomes 6. Demonstration 1 changes row 1 to [1,0,6,0,9,0,9].

Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours in the four cardinal directions. Demonstration 1 changes two row-1 zeros to 6 despite different immediate neighbours; demonstration 6 changes the rightmost zeros of rows 1 and 3 to 1. Directional context distinguishes these from unchanged zeros.

Use own colour with both row and column nonzero colour sets. In demonstration 1, 1 becomes 6 where both sets are {1,2,3}, while the row-4 1 stays 1. Demonstration 5 also changes zeros to 6 and a 2 to 3 according to their combined row and column sets.

Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours up, down, left and right. Demonstration 6 changes the top-right zero to 6 with nearest down and left colours both 2. Demonstration 8 changes row 2 column 0 to 8 with nearest up, down and right colours 2, 1 and 3.

Use own colour and coordinates modulo 3. In rows congruent to 1, zeros in columns congruent to 1 become 3. In rows congruent to 2, zeros become 7, 9 or 1 by column residue. Demonstration 3 turns its all-zero row 2 into [7,9,1,7,9,1,7].

Use own colour and zero-based coordinate parity. On even rows, all 2s become 0 and even-column 1s become 9. On odd rows, odd-column zeros become 1. Demonstration 1 changes row 2 to [9,0,0,3,0] and row 5 to [2,1,0,1,0].
